paragraphs: City news
Local craftsmen still weave carpets by hand using patterns
passed down for generations. The old harbour was rebuilt after
the storm and now hosts a small fish market every Sunday.
The market sells spices, dried fruit, olives and cheese made by
local shepherds. Swimming is not allowed when the red flag is
raised on the beach. Reservations are recommended for dinner,
especially on Friday and Saturday nights.
Shops in the village close early on Saturdays and stay closed on
Sundays. The concert has been moved to the cathedral because
of the heavy rain forecast for tonight. Lost property can be
collected from the information desk on the ground floor.
The castle garden contains more than four hundred kinds of
roses and a quiet pond with ducks. During the summer festival
the main square is closed to cars from noon until midnight.
A free shuttle bus runs between the hotel and the beach every
half hour. In the evening the narrow streets of the old quarter fill
with musicians and dancers. The ferry crossing takes about forty
minutes when the sea is calm.
The theatre was restored last year and now seats almost nine
hundred people. Trains to the airport leave every twenty minutes
from the second platform. Nobody remembered exactly when
the old clock in the square had stopped working.
The path along the cliffs is steep in places, so wear good shoes
and carry water. A cold wind blew from the north, and the
travellers pulled their coats more tightly around them. Please do
not feed the animals, as human food can make them seriously ill.
Bicycles can be rented at the station and returned at any of the
city's twelve stands. The observatory on the hill offers guided
tours of the night sky on clear evenings.
The road wound slowly through the forest until it reached a quiet
village by the lake. Visitors can climb the tower for a wide view
over the river and the rooftops.
Water from the mountain springs is clean and safe to drink
without boiling. The teacher asked the class to read the first
chapter again before the next lesson.
